title: State of Maharashtra v. Ankur Panwar (Preeti Rathi Acid Attack Case)
crime_type: Acid Attack Homicide / Stalking / Retaliatory Violence
court_or_authority: High Court of Bombay / Special Women's Court, Mumbai
legal_citation: Confirmation Case No. 1/2017; 2019 SCC OnLine Bom 1205; 2019 CriLJ 4652
source: High Court of Bombay Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/18491823)
ipc_sections: Section 326A IPC (Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid)
evidence: CCTV surveillance footage from Bandra Terminus platform showing a masked male carrying a container and boarding departing train
Train reservation and passenger chart records proving accused traveled on the same Garib Rath train from Delhi to Mumbai
Chemical forensic analysis identifying concentrated 98% commercial sulphuric acid residue on victim luggage and platform floor
Recovery of empty acid container with suspect's finger marks from New Delhi railway yard
Testimony of train co-passengers and victim family identifying suspect's physical silhouette and eye features
modus_operandi: Harbored extreme professional jealousy and resentment after victim was selected as a Lieutenant in the Military Nursing Service while he remained unemployed. Procured commercial battery acid in Delhi, concealed it in a vessel, shadowed the victim and her family aboard the train to Mumbai. As she stepped onto Platform No. 3 at Bandra Terminus, approached from behind, threw concentrated acid onto her face and chest, and fled on a moving local train.
personality_disorder: Clinical evaluation noted acute narcissistic entitlement, deep-seated resentment of female autonomy, obsessive jealousy, and explosive retaliatory aggression.
common_traits: Targeting young professional woman following career achievement
Obsessive stalking and inter-state surveillance across 1,400 km transit
Use of commercial corrosive chemical agent (Sulphuric acid)
Attack executed in crowded public railway junction
Immediate flight via urban commuter transport
summary: Historic Mumbai trial that set precedent for Section 326A IPC (introduced post-2013 Criminal Law Amendment Act). The Special Women's Court awarded the death sentence, which the Bombay High Court commuted to life imprisonment without remission, establishing stringent standards on acid procurement tracking.
